memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why didn't you come to me? Am I really not able to reward you?" "Well, I have come to you now," Balaam replied. "But I can't say whatever I please. I must speak only what God puts in my mouth." - Num 22:37-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak greets Balaam with a note of complaint. Why the delay? Did Balaam doubt that the king could reward him well? Balak assumes that money is the issue, that a richer offer will secure the outcome he wants. His whole worldview is built on the power of payment.

Balaam's reply, at least, contains a truth he has finally grasped. He tells Balak plainly that he cannot say whatever he pleases; he can only speak what God puts in his mouth. Whatever else is tangled in Balaam's heart, he now understands that the words are not his to control. God alone determines what will be spoken.

This is a lesson about where true authority lies. Balak thought he could buy a curse; Balaam had learned that no amount of silver could purchase God's words. The message would come from the Lord, not from the highest bidder. Human power meets its limit at the throne of God.

For us there is both warning and comfort. We cannot manipulate God to serve our agendas, however much we may wish to. But we can also rest knowing that God's purposes will not be overturned by wealth or influence. In Christ, God's word stands firm, unbought and unstoppable (Isa 55:11). His will, not the will of the powerful, prevails.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever try to bend God's will to fit your own agenda?
2. How does it comfort you that God's word cannot be bought or manipulated?
3. Where do you need to submit to God's word rather than your own desires?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, remind me that Your word cannot be bought or bent to my wishes. Help me to submit to Your purposes rather than trying to make You serve mine. Amen.
